platforms.name: Cambly
platforms.notes: Per-minute rate model. Cambly accepts tutors based in India (and is one of the more accessible platforms for Indian-based tutors).

platforms.name: UrbanPro
platforms.notes: Lead-based marketplace. Tutors pay for student leads (~₹100–₹300 per qualified lead) rather than commission per lesson.

platforms.name: Vedantu
platforms.notes: Heavily K-12-focused. Tutor revenue share varies by tier; ~70% to tutor at standard tier.

platforms.name: Chegg India (Q&A)
platforms.notes: Per-question payment, not per-hour. Asynchronous Q&A model — pays ₹50–₹200 per accepted answer depending on subject.

platforms.name: Filo
platforms.notes: On-demand 1:1 tutoring app. Per-minute pricing; tutor takes ~70-75%.

tax.self_employment_form: ITR-3 (business income) or ITR-4 / Sugam (presumptive scheme under Section 44ADA)
registration_steps: Get a PAN (Permanent Account Number) if you don't already — required for any tax filing.
Decide on your tax regime: New regime (above brackets, default from FY 2023-24) or Old regime (with deductions). New regime is usually simpler for most tutors.
Section 44ADA presumptive scheme: if professional gross receipts ≤ ₹50 lakh/year, you can declare 50% of receipts as deemed income — file ITR-4 instead of ITR-3, no detailed books required.
GST registration is required only if turnover exceeds ₹20 lakh/year (services). Most private tutors are well below this.
If you DO cross the GST threshold: register on https://www.gst.gov.in/, file monthly GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B (or GSTR-4 quarterly under composition scheme).
Income tax return due 31 July (for non-audit cases) — assessment year is the year following financial year (April–March).
Advance tax: if total tax liability for the year exceeds ₹10,000, you must pay in 4 instalments (15 June, 15 Sept, 15 Dec, 15 March). Section 44ADA filers have a single 15 March deadline.
tax.notes: The presumptive scheme under Section 44ADA is the simplest option for private tutors with gross receipts under ₹50 lakh — 50% of receipts deemed expenses, no books. Most independent tutors qualify for this. New tax regime brackets above are FY 2024-25; verify current year on incometax.gov.in.

background_check.name: Police Clearance Certificate (PCC) — local Police Commissioner's office
background_check.notes: Not legally required for private tutoring, but parents (especially for in-person tutoring of minors) increasingly request a PCC. Apply via the Passport Seva portal or directly at the local police commissioner's office. Fee ~₹500. Validity typically 6 months.

payment_methods.name: UPI (Unified Payments Interface)
payment_methods.notes: Free, instant, India-only. Default payment method for nearly all domestic tutoring transactions. Works via PhonePe, GPay, Paytm, BHIM, etc.

payment_methods.name: NEFT / IMPS / RTGS (bank transfer)
payment_methods.notes: Free or near-free domestic bank transfer. IMPS is instant, NEFT is batch-processed.

payment_methods.name: Razorpay (for invoicing)
payment_methods.notes: Useful if you want a payment-link to send parents. ~2% fee on UPI, ~2.5% on cards. Free tier available.

payment_methods.name: Wise
payment_methods.notes: Useful for receiving payments from international students. Inward USD/EUR/GBP arrives as INR at near-mid-market rate.

payment_methods.name: Stripe (international invoicing)
payment_methods.notes: Stripe is available in India in Beta — check eligibility. ~2% + ₹3 per domestic transaction.

insurance.notes: Professional indemnity / public liability is uncommon for individual private tutors in India but recommended for tutors of minors and for those running coaching classes from a fixed location. Annual premiums are modest (~₹2,000–₹8,000) for ₹10–25 lakh cover.
